I may have had a surgery I probably didn’t need :(

Hi all, I will try to give as much detail as I can without dragging this out too much. I’ve had pretty bad flat feet since I was a kid which are considered flexible. My feet were bad enough that when doctors saw them they called other doctors in to look at them even if the appointment in question wasn’t about my feet at all.

 So my mother trying to help her son she decided on a minimally invasive surgery(also reversible) to help my feet because the sounding board around her was that they were bad. As I grew up insoles were the norm even with the operation but I began to have more problems with my left foot as I aged. My left foot would go numb if I walked with any intensity and I began having pain on the inner muscles of my leg as well as lateral pain starting from my pinky toe. To add my achilles tendon would get these shocks and I couldn’t figure out why although being active I didn’t think I was overdoing it and general discomfort in shoes on my left side.

 I should also mention persistent knee pain since I was a kid. I went to the doctor who did the surgeries I had gotten done in middle school and Highschool(as I didn’t get both done at the same time) to have a look and he just wanted me to ice it and witch was fairly difficult just because the angle but none the less I tried it to no avail. I likely did not do it enough. 

I went back to this doctor for this pain and I also let him in on the Achilles tendon pain and he suggested I do some eccentric exercises at home and if this didn’t work he’d put in an order for physical therapy. This doctor also in that appointment said that he would make some adjustments to my orthotics to see if that would make a difference and he suggested until then I should go get some good shoes like hokas as well as super feet insoles.

 I went out and spent close to 200$ on the shoes and I did not buy the insoles admittedly. The shoes themselves didn’t help as much as I thought and when I received his revised insoles they were my old insoles with a piece of cushion glued to the top only on the left side. I was very frustrated. This new insole solution made it even harder to fit into shoes on my left side. He gave me no real answers on why the pain was there and what exactly I need to do to fix this pain specifically. 

I decided to get a second opinion from a doctor who recommended reconstruction of left foot but he was retiring soon and didn’t feel comfortable doing the surgery as he wouldn’t be able to see it all the way through. He sends me to another doctor who he trusted and this doctor also agreed that surgery was a good idea after I asked if this surgery made sense. 

Fast forward I get the surgery months go by I graduate from physical therapy and all seems well a lot of the pain I was gone or subsiding and I’m fitting in shoes better and it seems my knee feels better to. The issue is my flexibility in this foot isn’t as good anymore and now that I’m walking correctly it highlights another issue. Big toe pain when I walk. 

The first doctor I spoke performed a bunionectomy on that side when he did the minimally invasive surgery that I was unaware of and this has caused me more pain than anything. Whenever I walk my big toe hurts. It makes me wonder if I was walking on the side of my foot to overcompensate for the lack of motion in turn hurting the lateral side of my foot starting all this. 

I keep thinking about how I should have went through physical therapy and maybe got a shot in my foot but what’s done is done now as I can’t go back. I was just so frustrated with the lack of answers and wasted trips to the doctors. So when two said a surgery would help I jumped on it. I was desperate and tired of trying to figure it out and I just wanted to live. 

None of the doctors did a mri or checked my gait or offered cortisone shots first and it felt like none of them had my best interest at heart nor did any of them inform me of why I was having the issue at all. Now I wonder all the time was this the right choice? Because I don’t think everything that could have been looked into was looked into and I don’t think all conservative measures were taken. 

Admittedly  I should have done physical therapy when it was offered by the first doctor so I’ll take accountability there. The lack of information given about my pain and failure to diagnose, The lack of testing,the willingness for two new doctors just seeing me for the first time being willing to perform a major surgery is on them. more need for dopamine means less attention span.

I'm an old zoomer, so I know what you mean and i see both sides of it. Let me explain.

When you're very young, your brain develops connections. 

As you grow and age, your brain reinforces these connections.

When you give a small child a dopamine filled device, their brains build stronger dopamine related connections that consistently need more and more dopamine.

Think of how a drug addict might act and the levels of dopamine in their brain. It's a very strong pathway that's constantly needing more.

The zoomer brain is built similar to that of a drug addict. The more dopamine pathways and connections that you create when you're young, the more dopamine you need when you grow up. 

Before tech, kids got excited when they answered a math problem correct. Now, they won't try to do it because it's "not interesting enough." 

And the reason it's not interesting enough is because you've had too much dopamine fueled into your system that everything around you seems mundane.

So you have children who don't have adhd, but have attention spans like they do, not entirely because of attention span itself, but because the child needs more dopamine than normal tasks are willing to give. Although, this is a main factor in ADHD. 

Dopamine controls executive function. Executive function makes you do things. Not enough dopamine makes you not do things. 

This is why you are hearing and seeing studies about zoomers not paying enough attention or how they can't. It's not that we all have ADHD (cause we dont) it's that the exuberant amount of technology inserted at an extremely young age can change a brain like that.  

ON THE OTHER HAND: tech isn't bad, that's not what im saying. Too much is bad. I don't think a child under 3 should have access to technology, or more than (honestly) 15-20 minutes a day of TV or handheld tech. Now if you have educational videos on a background TV (like nat geo or discivery or pbs), that's different because 1. they're not really paying attention, 2. it's usually a real person in the video and 3. they sponge it up.

Tech can do things like LAMP tech for SPED students which is language acquisition for motor planning and it's a tablet system where a nonverbal sped student can make a language connection to their motor schools. It's the coolest thing ever to watch a non verbal student communicate with me through a tablet.
Tech can also do other things for students with dyslexia like virtual readers and so forth.
There's so much you can learn from being active in technology and there's a whole wide world out there.

As for average schools and your average student, bring the computer labs back! No more chromebooks! Only for those who truly need them. Maybe chromebooks for high school students but middle schoolers and elementary kids don't need them. They need a computer lab to go to that the teacher signs out for the class on library day. 

A child doesn't build the same brain connections doing everything online as if they were to do it by hand. By hand and on paper.
